summary.headline: Sharda Cropchem Q2 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR1,052 crore and PAT 23% to INR92 crore, despite a 5.1% volume decline.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 13% YoY to INR1,052 crore, driven by price, forex and mix (18.3% contribution) offsetting a 5.1% volume decline. EBITDA rose 18% to INR164 crore at a 15.6% margin, and gross margin expanded 140 bps to 35.9%. NAFTA (about 30% growth) and LATAM (agrochemical revenue up over 80%) offset a softer Europe, which management attributed to weather-led distributor caution. Management maintained FY27 revenue growth guidance of 10–15% and EBITDA margin of 18–20%. The company remains debt-free with INR846 crore of cash and liquid investments.

financial_highlights.change: +11% YoY; agrochemical +6% to INR1,755 crore, non-agro +40% to INR371 crore

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Largest market; saw slight moderation after an exceptionally strong FY26 as distributors restocked cautiously amid heat and drought. Q2 Europe gross margin about 41%. Management expects recovery in H2, the seasonally stronger period.

segments.name: NAFTA
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 30% YoY with significantly better margins; Q2 gross margin about 40%. Management says the margin gains are sustainable, citing good demand and lower availability.

segments.name: LATAM
segments.commentary: Agrochemical revenue up over 80% YoY; Q2 gross margin about 14%. Volume grew in LATAM per management's comments on NAFTA and LATAM, though the volume split was not stated for LATAM specifically.

segments.name: Non-agrochemical
segments.commentary: Revenue INR212 crore in Q2 (+68% YoY) and INR371 crore in H1 (+40%), driven mainly by conveyor and rubber belts. Margins fell in Q2 on higher transportation costs for conveyor belts.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at 10–15%.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 18–20%, supported by better product mix and H2 operating leverage.
Gross margin in H2 expected to hold or improve from Q2 level of 35.9%, per management.
Management said H2 EBITDA margin could be above 20% if the low end of 18% for the year is assumed.
FY27 planned capex of INR550–600 crore for product registrations; INR419 crore already spent in H1 per analyst's reading of the call.
Amortisation to stay elevated in H2 as capitalised registration intangibles are amortised over 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q2 revenue growth between forex, realisation and volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management restated 18.3% from price, forex and mix with a 5.1% volume decline. It did not provide the split between realisation and forex and offered to follow up offline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did registrations rise about 50 while the pipeline fell about 120 over 12 months?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there were no withdrawals; some registrations were discontinued and new ones came in. He linked the increase in H1 capex to US data compensation. Regional registration and pipeline numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: Will Europe margins return to the earlier high profitability levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said European profitability is likely to improve.

qa_highlights.question: Is an H2 EBITDA margin above 20% achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, it can be.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving non-agro growth and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly conveyor and rubber belts, driven by customers restocking after supply uncertainty and transport disruptions. Management did not say how long the trend will last.

qa_highlights.question: Why is depreciation and amortisation up, and does it lead revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said higher amortisation (5-year life) will continue in H2 and is tied to new registrations that should lift future revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin fall in H2 given oil and commodity pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 gross margins are expected to hold or go up.

risks_watch: Europe recovery depends on weather normalisation and distributor restocking; management has not quantified the H2 pick-up.
Registration timing is unpredictable (regulatory delays, new test requirements, US data compensation arbitration), so capex phasing could shift.
Analysts questioned the registration count versus the pipeline, which the management did not fully answer.
Volume decline continued in H1 (-3.5%); management expects normalisation in H2 but gave no volume guidance.
NAFTA margin sustainability depends on tight availability and demand, which may not last.
Freight costs from Hormuz and Red Sea routes are rising; EUR/USD near 1.12 is a forex sensitivity.
Non-agro margins fell in Q2 on conveyor-belt transport costs.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the headline numbers and the H2 recovery outlook, but evasive on granular questions: the realisation/forex split, the US registration breakup, and the registration pipeline decline were deferred offline. Management also called registration timing and regulatory outcomes "totally unpredictable."
key_quotes: We continue to maintain our FY27 revenue growth guidance to 10% to 15%.
Tariffs are not affecting agrochemical business at all.
So, it is very easy for us to pass on all the tariff increases to the customers.
We see this as a temporary weather-led impact rather than any change in underlying demand.
capex_capacity: Total product registrations stood at 3,044 as on 30 Sep 2026, with 946 applications in the pipeline (Europe 1,701 registrations / 548 pipeline; NAFTA 333 / 103; LATAM 760 / 155; Rest of World 250 / 140).
FY27 planned capex of INR550–600 crore for product registrations, stated by management as aimed at increasing registrations.

Management stated actual H1 capex of INR419 crore; analyst cited about INR400 crore for H1. Management said the US data compensation payment drove the H1 capex increase and that the breakup would be provided offline.

Registration timing described by management as unpredictable: government requirements change late, approvals get delayed, and repeat tests can be required. Data compensation dispute with US counterparty may go to arbitration, which management said is slow; management said the outcome was higher than its experts expected.

Analyst observed that registrations rose about 50 over 12 months while the pipeline fell about 120; management said no registrations were withdrawn, some were discontinued and new ones came in during H1.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth of 13% YoY in Q2 came from price, positive forex and product mix (18.3% contribution) with volume down 5.1%; H1 growth of 11% came from price, forex and mix (14.5%) with volume down 3.5%. Management did not split realisation from forex and offered to follow up offline.

Europe, the largest market, moderated after a strong FY26 as distributors restocked cautiously amid heat and drought in Central and Eastern Europe. Management called it temporary and weather-led and expects H2 recovery, with European profitability likely to improve.

NAFTA revenue grew about 30% YoY on better demand and lower availability; management said these margins are sustainable. Volume grew in NAFTA but not in Europe; LATAM agrochemical revenue rose over 80% YoY.

Non-agro growth (+68% in Q2, +40% in H1) was mainly conveyor and rubber belts, driven by customers restocking after supply uncertainty and transport problems. Management did not say how long this lasts; Q2 non-agro margins fell on higher conveyor-belt transport costs.

Pricing: management said agrochemical prices are improving, though the pace is below expectations and prices remain well below pre-COVID levels. Management said tariffs do not affect agrochemicals and that increases can be passed on to customers. Freight costs are rising due to Hormuz and Red Sea routes, but management said this does not affect performance.

Management said volumes were improving in October in Europe and LATAM, and expects H1 weakness to normalise in H2. It gave no volume guidance. Management said China availability and prices for products remain good. Management said Q2 gross margins by region were Europe about 41%, NAFTA about 40%, LATAM about 14%, Rest of World about 31%, and group 35.9%.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth of 10-15% (midpoint 12.5%) was held, backed by price/mix/forex (14.5% H1 contribution) and NAFTA/LATAM/non-agro demand, with volume down 3.5% in H1; no specific capacity additions were given, and the only capex is registration spend of INR550-600 crore rather than productive capacity.
